decisions.reason: The evening day-patient program extends the firm's core psychiatric offer, has its own web page, and is likely funded by health insurers, so early results are judged against modest aspirations and organisational slack lets the firm carry it.

The custom furniture carpentry draws on existing sheltered-workshop production know-how and serves the firm's inclusion mission, so a small revenue shortfall would not trigger problemistic search strong enough to drop it.
Outpatient sociotherapy is close to the firm's established offer and is reimbursable, though its weak web presence suggests uncertain uptake that the firm can still tolerate in its first year.
Senior living counseling is featured on the home page, fits rising eldercare demand, and costs little to run, so it likely meets aspirations as a feeder for the core care business.

The retail shop sells sheltered-workshop goods and supports participation goals, but it is only mentioned on the website and exposed to retail risk, making it the most likely candidate for a shortfall that would prompt search, though not yet enough to drop it.
